name: Fixed-pitch grid
summary: Every character takes one cell of the same width, so text forms columns without a separate grid and a position is a count of characters.
how: Give every glyph one advance width, 0.60 em in most fonts, or 10 or 12 characters an inch on a typewriter.
Align columns with spaces and set tables, code and forms on the cell grid.
On a screen, size the layout in cells: 80 columns by 24 rows is the classic terminal.

origin.note: The Sholes and Glidden typewriter by E. Remington and Sons moves the carriage one fixed step for each key, so its type must be monospaced.

adoptions.via: Typewriter faces, then Courier for IBM in 1955.
Video terminals such as the DEC VT100 draw the whole screen as a grid of 80 by 24 character cells.
